title: What is Azure App Service
description: Understand App Service plans, deployment slots, and how ASP.NET Core apps run in Azure.

data.text: Azure App Service is a managed platform for hosting web apps, REST APIs, and mobile back ends. You bring your ASP.NET Core binaries, and Azure manages the operating system, runtime, and scaling.
An App Service plan defines the compute resources: CPU, memory, and number of instances. Multiple apps can share one plan.
Deployment slots are live apps with their own hostnames. You can deploy to a staging slot, test it, then swap it into production without downtime.

data.title: Why slots matter
data.text: Slots let you validate real traffic behavior before affecting users. Swapping also preserves the production app's settings if you configure slot settings correctly.
How ASP.NET Core Runs on App Service

items: App Service detects the ASP.NET Core app and runs it behind IIS or as a standalone process
Port binding is handled by the platform; your app should listen on the port provided by `ASPNETCORE_URLS` or `PORT`
Logs, environment variables, and mounted paths are injected by App Service

items.question: Do I need IIS knowledge?
items.answer: No. App Service abstracts IIS for ASP.NET Core. You deploy the app, and Azure runs the published output.

items.question: Can I run multiple apps on one plan?
items.answer: Yes. Apps on the same plan share compute resources, which reduces cost for smaller workloads.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: App Service is a managed host for web apps and APIs
Plans define compute; apps can share a plan
Your ASP.NET Core app runs as published output with platform-managed networking
data.takeaway: App Service is the fastest way to move an ASP.NET Core project from localhost to a production URL.
